{{Short description|American organization}}
The '''American Epidemiological Society''' is an American honorary society dedicated to [[epidemiology]]. It was established in 1927, and has held annual meetings since 1968.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Paul|first1=O|title=The last twenty-five years of the American Epidemiological Society: 1972-1996.|journal=American Journal of Epidemiology|date=1 July 1998|volume=148|issue=1|pages=104–30|pmid=9663413|doi=10.1093/oxfordjournals.aje.a009550|doi-access=}}</ref> It is the oldest epidemiology organization in the United States.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=McKeown|first1=RE|last2=Weed|first2=DL|last3=Kahn|first3=JP|last4=Stoto|first4=MA|title=American College of Epidemiology Ethics Guidelines: foundations and dissemination.|journal=Science and Engineering Ethics|date=April 2003|volume=9|issue=2|pages=207–14|pmid=12774653|url=http://www.acepidemiology.org/sites/default/files/ACEGuidelinesSEEEv9n2p207.pdf|doi=10.1007/s11948-003-0008-y|s2cid=46612519 |access-date=2016-02-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305230744/http://www.acepidemiology.org/sites/default/files/ACEGuidelinesSEEEv9n2p207.pdf|archive-date=2016-03-05|url-status=dead}}</ref> Past members of the society have included [[Wade H. Frost]], [[Alexander Langmuir]], [[Jonas Salk]] and [[Abraham Lilienfeld]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.depauw.edu/news-media/latest-news/details/17736/ | title=Kenrad Nelson '54 Elected President of American Epidemiological Society | work=DePauw University | date=29 June 2006 | accessdate=27 February 2016}}</ref>
